A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BUTTON research. Their text, figures, tables, mathematical notation, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original Llama3 and Qwen2 evaluations on GTA and Tool-Query, component ablations, data-scaling experiments, and dataset statistics.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds an analysis of generated function-name frequencies in Appendix B.3.

M1.justification: The bottom-up task composition, function generation, multi-agent trajectory generation, and parallel-calling procedures remain unchanged. Clarifying that function definitions are synthesized and supplying existing ablation prompts do not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain BUTTONInstruct, OpenHermes-2.5 training data, and GTA and Tool-Query evaluation coverage. Naming glaive-function-calling-v2 and ToolLLama as scenario sources in v2 discloses provenance without establishing newly added data coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same GPT-4o, GPT-4-Turbo, GPT-3.5-Turbo, and Llama3/Qwen2 instruction-model comparators. The bottom-up and top-down ablation configurations are also retained.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model sizes, metrics, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged, including 209 GTA end-to-end queries and the Tool-Query answer-containment check. Appendix C.3 newly documents prompts for existing ablations rather than reporting revised experimental settings.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.3 and Figure 4 analyze dataset diversity through the first and second words of generated function names. Existing component ablations, data scaling, parallel-calling analysis, and case studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new descriptive function-frequency chart adds no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 4 adds results describing generated function-name frequencies. Numerical entries in Tables 2–4, the ablation results in Figure 3, and the parallel-calling outcomes are unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions of scenarios, tasks, function sets, instruction tuples, and trajectories remain mathematically equivalent. Neither version introduces additional formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that BUTTON constructs compositional instruction data that improves multi-turn function calling and planning. The pipeline contribution, 8,000-example dataset, and claimed empirical effectiveness retain the same scope.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 newly interprets the function-name distribution as consistent with everyday tasks. Existing explanations of planning improvements and limitations concerning data verification and parallel-calling evaluation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 identifies the scenario seed datasets, while new Appendix C.3 supplies the exact bottom-up ablation prompt and parallel/nonparallel top-down ablation prompts. These improve documentation of existing procedures; training hyperparameters, hardware, and data-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including C-Pack, TaskBench, WizardMath, and Qwen2.5 reports, and removes the differential-privacy works by Lin et al. (2023) and Xie et al. (2024). The central positioning relative to compositional instruction tuning and function-calling datasets remains stable.

P1.justification: The opening introduction and related-work paragraphs receive targeted rewrites, terminology is clarified, and appendix subsections and cross-references are updated. The main narrative and section order are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the Figure 4 sunburst chart and boxed ablation prompts, repositions Table 1 and Figure 2, shortens some captions, and adds conference headers. Existing Figures 1–3 use identical graphics, and the performance-table structures remain intact.

improvement.justification: Identifying scenario sources in Appendix A.1 and supplying exact ablation prompts in Appendix C.3 reduce reproducibility gaps in v1. The function-distribution analysis modestly improves dataset characterization. These are useful, localized gains; the central experimental evidence and conclusions remain unchanged.
